intro: Zakat is an obligation Allah placed on wealthy Muslims, returned to the poor among them. It is an act of obedience with many benefits for the giver and society.
rate: Zakat is 2.5% of wealth that reaches the nisab and is held for a full Hijri year

tabDesc.livestock: Zakat on camels, cattle and sheep

belowNisab: The amount is below the nisab, so no zakat is due until it reaches it.
invalid: Please enter a valid non-negative number

money.goldPrice: Current price of 1 g of gold (24k)
money.nisabInfo: The nisab for money equals the value of 85 g of pure (24k) gold. Once your money reaches it and a full Hijri year passes, 2.5% is due.
money.notes: Nisab is the minimum amount of wealth a Muslim must own before zakat becomes due: the value of 85 grams of gold or 595 grams of silver, based on their current market price. If your money or assets reach the nisab and stay with you for a full lunar year, 2.5% of them is due as zakat. The gold nisab is usually recommended for cash.

gold.notes:
18 karat gold nisab: 113 grams, valued at the daily price per gram.
21 karat gold nisab: 97 grams, valued at the daily price per gram.
24 karat gold nisab: 85 grams, valued at the daily price per gram.
Silver nisab: 595 grams of silver, valued at the daily price per gram.

livestock.notWorkingDesc: They are not used for ploughing, irrigation or transport for profit.

explain.conditions: Zakat on livestock is due only if they graze freely, a full Hijri year has passed, and they are not working animals used for ploughing or irrigation.
explain.sheepBelow: The nisab for sheep starts at 40 head; below that no zakat is due.
explain.sheep1: From 40 to 120 sheep, the zakat is one sheep (one or two years old).
explain.sheep2: From 121 to 200 sheep, the zakat is two sheep.
explain.sheep3: From 201 to 399 sheep, the zakat is three sheep.
explain.sheep100: From 400 sheep upward, one sheep is due for every 100 (e.g. 400 sheep: 4 sheep).
explain.cowsBelow: The nisab for cattle starts at 30 head; below that no zakat is due.
explain.cows30: From 30 to 39 cattle, the zakat is one tabi' (a calf that completed one year).
explain.cows40: From 40 to 59 cattle, the zakat is one musinnah (a cow that completed two years).
explain.cows60: From 60 cattle upward, one tabi' is due for every 30 and one musinnah for every 40.
explain.camelsBelow: The nisab for camels starts at 5 head; below that no zakat is due.
explain.camels5: From 5 to 24 camels, one sheep is due for every 5 camels.
explain.camels25: From 25 to 35 camels, the zakat is one bint makhad (a she-camel in its second year).
explain.camels36: From 36 to 45 camels, the zakat is one bint labun (a she-camel in its third year).
explain.camels46: From 46 to 60 camels, the zakat is one hiqqah (a she-camel in its fourth year).
explain.camels61: From 61 to 75 camels, the zakat is one jadha'ah (a she-camel in its fifth year).
explain.camels76: From 76 to 90 camels, the zakat is two bint labun.
explain.camels91: From 91 to 120 camels, the zakat is two hiqqah.
explain.camels121: Above 120 camels, one bint labun is due for every 40 and one hiqqah for every 50.
explain.camels121Multi: Above 120 camels, one bint labun is due for every 40 and one hiqqah for every 50. Your count fits more than one combination, so any of them may be given.

livestock.notes:
• Livestock zakat covers camels, cattle and sheep.
• A full Hijri year must pass while owning the nisab.
• Sa'imah animals feed by grazing freely on open pasture.
• Animals fed with bought fodder all year, or used as working animals in farming or transport, are exempt.

crops.notes:
• Zakat is due on grains and fruits that are measured and stored, such as wheat, rice, dates and raisins.
• There is no zakat on vegetables and fresh fruit that are not stored long.
• The nisab is 5 awsuq (about 653 kg) of cleaned grain.
• Zakat is paid on the day of harvest, as Allah says: ﴿وَءَاتُوا۟ حَقَّهُۥ یَوۡمَ حَصَادِهِۦۖ ﴾.
